title: One command moves every machine to the manifest's set, verifies each, and rolls back on a red e2e

story.i_want_to: run release/rollout.sh once and have every fleet machine install the set's runner and chg from the loopctl repo, prove it joined at that set, and see the e2e pass
story.so_that: no machine is left on an old part or on the archived repos, and a bad set is undone without hand work

rationale: PRD R7: 'One command rolls the fleet to that set and verifies each machine.' Today each part is installed per machine from its own repo's checkout: runner rel/install.sh builds from the checkout it sits in (rel/install.sh, repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/..")), chg scripts/install.sh builds or downloads into ~/.local/bin/chg and install-system.sh writes /usr/local/bin/chg on CI hosts, and infra's chg jobs pull ~/workspace/chg (infra scripts/jobs/chg-job.sh, scripts/runner-deps.sh:285). After US-52.11 archives those repos, those checkouts stop moving. This story is also how existing installs switch source: the same prefixes, units and config, built from a tag of this repo.

acceptance_criteria.description: release/install-machine.sh <set>, on one machine, clones or fetches mkreyman/loopctl into ~/.local/share/loopctl-factory/sets/<set> at tag factory-<set>, installs that tree's .tool-versions toolchains with asdf when missing, and swaps ~/.local/share/loopctl-factory/current to it with a symlink rename; it keeps the three newest sets, and two concurrent runs are serialised by an mkdir lock, the second exiting 75 'busy'.

Before replacing the runner, install-machine.sh sets the running runner draining (bin/loopctl_runner rpc calling LoopctlRunner.Control.set_draining/2, runner control.ex:420) and waits up to 60 minutes for its in-flight dispatches to reach zero; on timeout it undrains it, leaves the runner and chg unchanged and reports status runner_busy.

install-machine.sh installs the runner with current/runner/rel/install.sh into the existing prefix ~/.local/share/loopctl-runner, unit loopctl-runner.service or com.loopctl.runner and config ~/.config/loopctl-runner/runner.json, rewriting a selection_replay entry keyed mkreyman/chg to mkreyman/loopctl with chg/-prefixed paths; it installs chg with current/chg/scripts/install.sh into ~/.local/bin/chg, and with install-system.sh too where /usr/local/bin/chg already exists.

install-machine.sh prints one JSON line {host, set, status, runner_version, chg_version} where status is ok only when chg --version (both installs where two exist) names the set's chg version and the tag's commit, and the runner's joined.json (US-52.8) is newer than the restart and names release_set <set>; a machine already at the set prints status unchanged and restarts nothing.

release/rollout.sh first requires /.well-known/loopctl release.set to equal the manifest's set and npm view loopctl-mcp-server@<mcp version> to exist, then runs install-machine.sh on each host of FLEET_MACHINES in turn over ssh under nice, continues past an unreachable host (status unreachable), and prints one summary table.

When every host is ok or unchanged, rollout.sh dispatches .github/workflows/e2e.yml and waits for it; if e2e fails, it runs install-machine.sh <previous set> on every host it moved, prints the e2e run URL and exits 1; with any host failed or unreachable it skips e2e and exits 1.

In infra, scripts/jobs/chg-job.sh and scripts/runner-deps.sh read chg from ~/.local/share/loopctl-factory/current/chg (no git pull of their own), and systemd/infra-chg-loop.service passes --repo mkreyman/loopctl, in a pull request to mkreyman/infra merged before US-52.11 archives mkreyman/chg.

test_cases.name: set checkout, symlink swap, retention and lock (ExUnit, shell under test)
preconditions: a temp HOME; a local bare repo standing in for mkreyman/loopctl with tags factory-1..factory-4; asdf, runner and chg installers stubbed on PATH
steps: hold the lock dir and run again
expected_results: current points at sets/4; only sets 2..4 remain; the locked run exits 75 printing busy

test_cases.name: drain wait and runner_busy (shell under test)
preconditions: a bin/loopctl_runner stub answering rpc with in_flight counts from a script file
steps: counts stuck at 1 with the wait shortened by LOOPCTL_FACTORY_DRAIN_S=3
expected_results: the install proceeds after 0; then status runner_busy, set_draining(false) called, the installer stubs never called

test_cases.name: installs into the existing prefixes and verifies the join (shell under test)
preconditions: temp HOME with runner.json holding selection_replay {"mkreyman/chg": {...}}; /usr/local/bin/chg simulated by LOOPCTL_FACTORY_SYSTEM_BIN; stubs writing joined.json with release_set from an env var
expected_results: status ok, both chg installs called, runner.json re-keyed with chg/ paths; then status failed join_set_mismatch; then status unchanged with no installer call

test_cases.name: rollout preflight, unreachable host, e2e rollback (shell under test)
preconditions: stubs for curl (well-known), npm, ssh (per-host scripted outcome) and gh (workflow run and watch with a scripted conclusion)
steps: hosts a, b ok and e2e failing
expected_results: exit 1 before any ssh; exit 1 with b unreachable and no gh workflow run; install-machine.sh 1 sent to a and b, exit 1 printing the run URL

test_cases.name: infra reads chg from the factory tree (infra's tests)
steps: grep the three files for workspace/chg and mkreyman/chg
run chg-job.sh with a temp HOME holding a fake current/chg
expected_results: no match; the job runs the fake tree's bin/ without a git pull

technical_notes: Runner installer: runner rel/install.sh (prefix ~/.local/share/loopctl-runner, releases/<stamp>, current symlink, history, mkdir lock .install.lock, keeps 3 releases, preflight via bin/loopctl_runner eval "LoopctlRunner.Application.preflight()", systemd user unit loopctl-runner.service or launchd com.loopctl.runner). It builds from its own checkout, so running it from sets/<n>/runner builds the set's runner into the same prefix: this is the source switch, with no unit or config change. Draining: LoopctlRunner.Control.set_draining/2 at runner lib/loopctl_runner/control.ex:420; in-flight count from the same rpc.

chg installers: chg scripts/install.sh (default dest ~/.local/bin/chg, then install-elixir-adapter.sh --all-installed) and scripts/install-system.sh (/usr/local/bin/chg and /usr/local/share/chg adapters, CI hosts). KB: chg has two installs per machine (~/.local/bin and /usr/local/bin), and a non-interactive PATH can find either, so both are verified.

Hosts: FLEET_MACHINES in claude-config hooks/lib/fleet-name.sh:35 (minis mac-mini beelink blockit nuc x1 ryzen), read by sourcing that file. beelink and nuc need '. "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh"' in a non-interactive ssh (USER.md), so install-machine.sh sources it when present. Each host runs under nice -n 10 (memory: batch work on fleet boxes runs niced).

Server preflight: /.well-known/loopctl release (US-52.7). MCP: not installed per machine in this release; machines launch loopctl-mcp-server@latest through claude-config bin/loopctl-mcp.sh, so the rollout checks npm has the set's version and US-52.8's refusal covers a stale one.

e2e: gh workflow run e2e.yml -R mkreyman/loopctl, then gh run watch on that run id (US-52.9). Rollback reinstalls the previous set (manifest set - 1, still in sets/ because three are kept), which is backward compatible by US-52.8's rule.

infra (separate repo mkreyman/infra): scripts/jobs/chg-job.sh (CHG=${INFRA_CHG_DIR:-$HOME/workspace/chg}, pulls master --ff-only), scripts/runner-deps.sh:285 (chg_src=${CHG_SRC:-$HOME/workspace/chg}), scripts/systemd/infra-chg-loop.service:20 (--repo mkreyman/chg). A released fix now reaches these jobs at the next rollout, not at the next merge (defaults).
No new table, context, route or tool.
non_goals: Pinning the MCP package per machine: release 8.
Rolling the server: the master deploy in ci.yml stays its only path.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.10.5: an unreachable host is reported unreachable and the rollout continues to the next; the run then exits 1 and skips e2e, so a partial fleet is never declared done.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.10.1: which set a machine runs is the current symlink under ~/.local/share/loopctl-factory, swapped by rename; the runner's own release history stays in its prefix.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.10.4: a re-run on a machine already at the set reports unchanged and restarts nothing; AC-52.10.1: a concurrent run exits busy.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.10.2: a busy runner is waited on for at most 60 minutes, then left untouched and reported runner_busy.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.10.4: each machine proves it reached the set through joined.json, written by the runner after loopctl admitted its join.

defaults: Hosts are rolled one at a time, niced (owner may parallelise).
A failed e2e rolls every moved host back to the previous set.
infra's chg jobs run the released tree, not chg master.
definition_of_done: release/rollout.sh run once after the epic merges prints ok or unchanged for every reachable host and a green e2e run.
runner_pool shows every connected runner at the manifest's runner_version.
